name: THE COUNTER REVOLUTION
notes: Wheatstone row correctly hedges (Christie devised the bridge) and Dewar/Thermos checks out; softened 'a pupil of Galileo' to 'Galileo's assistant in his final months', which is what Torricelli actually was.

name: RATE EXPECTATIONS
notes: Richter/Mohs/Scoville/Apgar attributions verified; replaced the Fujita row with Beaufort (Irish-born, 1805, 0-12) because n1-sci names the Fujita scale outright in a clue.

name: PIGMENT OF THE IMAGINATION
notes: Rayleigh, Newton's indigo, CMYK 'key plate' and metamerism all verified; shares spectrum territory with PRISM BREAK in the same file.

name: PRISM BREAK
notes: Secondary-rainbow reversal, Cherenkov glow and Fraunhofer (Bavarian optician who catalogued the lines) are all accurate.

name: FACET THE FACTS
notes: Opal, corundum, beryl, heat-treated citrine and Moissan's Arizona silicon carbide all check out; clean ladder and strong hooks.

name: IGNEOUS IS BLISS
notes: Every fact holds (Siccar Point, Alvarez iridium, Mohorovicic 1909), but the name promises igneous and only obsidian delivers — marble is metamorphic by the clue's own wording.

name: WHISK ASSESSMENT
notes: Lecithin, cabbage indicator, ceviche denaturation, Nahuatl-rooted nixtamalization and cream of tartar from wine barrels are all correct.

name: REPEATABLE OFFENSES
notes: Eratosthenes, Eddington at Principe, Millikan, Michelson-Morley and Cavendish's 1798 torsion balance verified; textbook ladder.

name: TEST SUBJECTS
notes: Pavlov, Mischel, Miller, Hershey-Chase blender and Redi/Spallanzani all accurate; second famous-experiments category in one file is a mild repeat.

name: SOUNDING OFF
notes: Replaced the Trieste row — n1-people's clue names 'the bathyscaphe Trieste' — with Hess's echo-sounded guyots, named for Arnold Guyot; other rows (Franklin, thermocline, Tharp) verified.

name: CULTURE CLUB
notes: Lactobacillus, Penicillium roqueforti, Taq from Yellowstone, Marshall's 1984 self-infection and koji Aspergillus all verified.

name: THE FRAUD SQUAD
notes: Piltdown orangutan jaw, 1989 cold fusion, 1869 Cardiff Giant, the Sun's 1835 moon hoax and Blondlot's N-rays are all accurate and well hedged.
